html:
Dominica became independent from Britain on 3 November 1978, as a republic within the Commonwealth. Patrick John was the first prime minister.

Britain had held the island since the Seven Years' War, though French influence stayed strong: many people speak a French based Creole, and most are Catholic. Bananas grown on small farms replaced sugar and limes as the main crop in the 20th century.

The first years were rough: Hurricane David in 1979, the fall of Patrick John, and two failed coup plots, one involving American and Canadian mercenaries in 1981. Eugenia Charles led the country from 1980 to 1995 and backed the invasion of Grenada in 1983.
sum: Dominica became independent from Britain on 3 November 1978, as a republic within the Commonwealth. Patrick John was the first prime minister.
